Compare the contents beside this document with the headings in it.

## Listed without its subsections {toc-depth=1}

The heading is in the contents; the one below it is not.

### Hidden by the parent

Inherited from the cascade.

## Overriding the cascade {toc-depth=1}

### Widened again {toc-depth=2}

A heading with its own attribute takes over the cascade for its subtree.

#### Listed because of the override

## Out of the contents entirely {toc-depth=0}

Absent from the contents, and unnumbered. Its subsections go with it.

## Notes

The depth is counted from the heading that carries it.
Quarto's own `toc-depth` is applied first, so a heading attribute can narrow what would have been listed but cannot widen it beyond that limit; this document raises it to `5`.

Set `extensions.toc-depth.default` to annotate only the exceptions.

Full documentation: <https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-toc-depth/>.
